subject: SLA metrics and dashboard access for procurement review
messages:
From: Maya Singh <procurement@acme-health.com>

Subject: Procurement questionnaire: how you measure uptime/latency & access to metrics

Marcus —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement has a few follow-up items for our security and IT audit team focused on the SLA and how you demonstrate meeting your SLOs. High level asks:

- How do you measure availability and which regions are covered?
- How is latency measured (p50/p95/p99) and what synthetic/real-user monitoring do you run?
- Can we get temporary read-only access to the metrics dashboard for the audit?
- If you make an exception to an SLA (credit or remediation), how is that documented and who signs off?

Attaching the standard Acme procurement questionnaire — we’d appreciate a response by EOD Monday so we can move to legal.

Thanks,
Maya Singh
Head of Procurement — Acme Health
procurement@acme-health.com

Attachment: acme-procurement-slo-questions.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <procurement@acme-health.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Feb 2026 09:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire: how you measure uptime/latency & access to metrics

Hi Maya —

Appreciate the clear list. I’m including Lauren (Customer Success) and Stephanie (Product — SRE interface) to provide the technical detail and set up access. Short answers up front, full responses attached: redwood-slo-metrics-2026-02.pdf.

- Availability: We measure service availability at the API level per-region (us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1) using both internal request logs and a synthetic probing fleet. Our production SLA is 99.95% monthly availability for the Hosted API.
- Latency: We record p50/p95/p99 for end-to-end request completion (request accepted -> final token returned) and for token-generation time (per-token). Reports separate cold-start and steady-state. Typical Hosted API p95 is 220ms for responses <512 tokens in us-east-1.
- Monitoring: Internal metrics use Prometheus + Cortex; synthetic checks run on an hourly cadence across zones. We also compute customer-specific SLOs in our console and persist historical percentiles for 13 months.
- Dashboard access: We can provide temporary read-only dashboard links (expiration + IP-restriction) and a one-time exported CSV of raw SLO windows.
- SLA exceptions: Exception requests (credits, targeted remediation) are handled by Product + Finance; we keep an audit record that includes incident timeline, capacity/trace logs, and the final credit calculation. Exceptions require sign-off from the Head of Product and Finance for credits >$25k.

We’ve attached the SLO evidence pack and a short invite token file with the temporary-dashboard link. Lauren — can you propose a 30-min window for a walkthrough with Acme IT audit this week?

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-slo-metrics-2026-02.pdf (application/pdf), dashboard-readonly-invite.txt (text/plain)

From: Daniel Park <it-audit@acme-health.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 31 Feb 2026 11:23:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire: how you measure uptime/latency & access to metrics

Marcus / Lauren —

Thanks for the packet. A couple of clarifying items from the audit team:

1) When you say "per-region" availability, do you calculate SLOs per-customer or per-backend-region only? We need to know if Acme's traffic is measured separately (we run across multiple regions).

2) For alerting: do we get email/SMS/Slack alerts for SLO breaches? Can alerts be routed to our PagerDuty (we have a procurement-facing PagerDuty project for vendor incidents)?

3) For the temporary dashboard: we require a list of user accounts (emails) and an expiry date. Also preferable: IP allowlist to our audit gateway.

4) Lastly, on exception documentation: please include the template you use to record incident impact and credit calculations (we have an exceptions review board).

Appreciate a quick confirmation on those four so our legal team can finalize.

Daniel Park
IT Audit — Acme Health
it-audit@acme-health.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <it-audit@acme-health.com>, Maya Singh <procurement@acme-health.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 31 Feb 2026 15:47:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire: how you measure uptime/latency & access to metrics

Hi Daniel / Maya —

Thanks — answered inline below and attaching the SLO evidence template you asked for.

1) SLO scope: We publish both per-region and per-customer SLOs. For Hosted customers we also compute customer-scoped windows (the console shows Acme-specific p99/p95 across the last 30/90/365-day windows). If Acme routes traffic to multiple regions, we can present both the aggregated view and region-by-region breakdown.

2) Alerting: We support webhook integration (recommended) and direct PagerDuty routing. Alerts can be sent to email or a dedicated Slack channel. For procurement audits we typically enable a read-only alert forwarding to the customer’s PagerDuty team (no escalation actions from our side unless the incident crosses an internal SLO).

3) Dashboard access: We will provision two read-only accounts for the audit (one for procurement, one for IT audit). Proposed expiry: 14 days. We will also configure IP allowlist to the Acme audit gateway. Please confirm the two emails you want provisioned and the public IPs (or CIDR) to allow. A short invite token has been posted to the link below.

4) Exception template: attached. For credits, our template includes incident timeline, root cause summary, affected customers, uptime windows, and credit calculation. Exception approvals: Product lead + Finance; credits >$25k require Exec sign-off. For smaller credits we can do delegated approval.

Next steps:
- Maya: confirm the two audit users and expiry (we set 14 days by default).
- Daniel: confirm IPs/CIDR for allowlist.
- Marcus / Stephanie: schedule 30-min walkthrough (we can do Wed 10:00–10:30 or Thu 13:00–13:30 ET).

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
